questions.question: Which of the following is the earliest literary record of Indian culture?
questions.solution:
Rigveda
There are four Vedas: Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, and Atharvaveda. The Rigveda is the oldest among them and the earliest literary record of Indian culture.

questions.question:
Match the ancient names of rivers with their present names:
(A) Asikni1. Beas
(B) Vitasta2. Jhelum
(C) Purushni3. Ravi
(D) Vipasha4. Chenab
questions.solution:
A-4, B-2, C-3, D-1
Ancient names of Indian Rivers:
  • Vitasta - Jhelum
  • Purushni - Ravi
  • Shatudri - Satluj
  • Vipasha - Beas
  • Sadanira - Gandak
  • Drishdvati - Ghashara
  • Asikni - Chenab

questions.question: Which of the following Vedas is found in two recensions, black and white, and is full of rituals to be performed publicly or individually?
questions.solution:
Yajurveda
Notable Upanishads of Yajurveda - Brihadaranyaka, Isha, Taittriya, Katha, and Maithri.

questions.question: In which of the following Vedas was Dasarajna war (the war of ten kings) mentioned?
questions.solution:
Rigveda (Book of Mantras)
Dasarajna war was fought between King Sudas of the Bharata tribe and a confederation of ten tribes, including the Puru, Yadu, Turvasa, Anu, Druhyu, Alina, Paktha, Bhalanas, Shiva, and Vishanin. The battle took place on the banks of the Parushni (Ravi) river.

questions.question: The main (chief) social unit of the Aryans was
questions.solution:
Jana (Tribes)
  • Gana - Tribal or clan based assemblies
  • Parishad - A small body similar to Samitis/sabhas consisting exclusively of Brahmins
  • Rajan - A kind of Chief or King

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Vedas:
1. Rig Veda is the oldest Veda and contains hymns mainly dealing with magic spells and charms.
2. Sama Veda is mainly a collection of chants and musical notations.
3. Atharva Veda contains a collection of magic spells and charms to ward off evil spirits and diseases.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
2 and 3 only
Rig Veda does not deal with magic spells and charms. Rig Veda has about 1,028 hymns (suktas) and 10,600 verses (richas). These hymns are mainly dedicated to various deities such as Indra, Agni, Varuna, Soma, Usha, etc.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Indian philosophy:
1. The Purva Mimansa school of philosophy was founded by Jaimini.
2. Kapila is regarded as the founder of the Samkhya school of philosophy.
3. Patanjali is associated with the Yoga school of philosophy.
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
1, 2 and 3
  • Purva Mimansa (Prior Study) also known as Dharma Mimamsa and Karma Mimamsa - founded by Jaimini
  • Samkhya - founded by Kapila
  • Yoga - associated with Patanjali
  • Badarayana - Author of Brahma Sutra or Vedanta Sutra
  • Vyasa - Author of the Mahabharata, Vedas and Puranas
The six principal Hindu darshans are Samkhya, Yoga, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Mimamsa, and Vedanta.

questions.question: India was named 'Bharat' after the name of the Bharat clan. In which of the following Vedas is this clan first mentioned?
questions.solution:
Rigveda
There are 1028 Suktas in 10 Mandals (Chapters).

questions.question: The language of the Aryan texts was:
questions.solution:
Sanskrit
Sanskrit was the first language spoken in India. Ardhamagadhi Prakrit was a Middle Indo-Aryan language. Prakrit is a group of vernacular Middle Indo-Aryan languages spoken in India between the third and seventh century BCE.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Rigvedic deities:
(a) Agni was worshipped as the fire-god during the Rigvedic period.
(b) Sindhu was regarded as a river goddess in the Rigveda.
(c) Usha was worshipped as the goddess of night.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
(A) and (B) only
Usha was worshipped as the goddess of dawn, not night.

questions.question: In the Rig Veda there is a hymn in the form of a dialogue between Sage Vishvamitra and two rivers that were worshipped as goddesses. Which are these rivers?
questions.solution:
Beas and Sutlej
The most prominent river in the Rig Veda is Saraswati.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the 'Gotra' practice in ancient India is true?
questions.option_1: Men and women were expected to marry within the same gotra.
questions.option_2: People belonging to the same gotra were regarded as descendants of the person after whom the gotra was named.
questions.option_3: Women retained their father's gotra after marriage.
questions.option_4: Each gotra was named after a famous king.
questions.solution:
People belonging to the same gotra were regarded as descendants of the person after whom the gotra was named
Gotra originally referred to the seven lineage segments of the Brahmanas (priests), who trace their derivation from seven ancient seers: Atri, Bharadvaja, Brhigu, Gotama, Kashyapa, Vasishtha, and Vishvamitra.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Purusha Sukta:
1. Purusha Sukta is a hymn from Rigveda.
2. It is dedicated to Lord Shiva, described as the great Purusha.
3. Purusha Sukta is one of the Pancha Suktam, which includes Vishnu Suktam, Sri Suktam, Bhu Suktam, and Nila Suktam.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
1 and 3 only
Statement 2 is incorrect because Purusha Sukta is dedicated to Lord Vishnu, not Lord Shiva.

questions.question: The Jain temple at Pattadakal was built by
questions.solution:
Rashtrakuta
Other temples made by Rashtrakutas - The Kailasanatha Temple in Ellora, the Navalinga Temples in Pattadakal.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Jain Tirthankaras:
(A) Ayodhya is recognized as the birthplace of the first Tirthankara, Rishabhdhev.
(B) Ayodhya is also the birthplace of the fourth Tirthankara, Abhinandannath.
(C) Varanasi is the birthplace of the first and fourth Tirthankaras.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
(A) and (B) only
  • Rishabhdhev, the first Jain Tirthankara, was born in Ayodhya
  • Abhinandannath, the fourth Jain Tirthankara, was also born in Ayodhya
  • Varanasi is recognized as the birthplace of three Jain Tirthankaras: 23rd Tirthankara Parshvanatha, 7th Tirthankara Suparshvanatha and 11th Tirthankara Shreyansanatha

questions.question: Which of the following describes the Medhi part in Buddhist structure?
questions.option_1: The circular terrace between the railing and dome
questions.option_2: Ceremonial gateways in front of stupas
questions.option_3: A low wall to enclose the structure
questions.option_4: The umbrella-shaped structure placed at the top of the structure
questions.solution:
The circular terrace between the railing and dome
All forms of Buddhist architecture include three primary structures: vihara, stupa, and chaitya-ghra.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct in context of Buddhist architecture?
i. The Uddeshika stupa was created as a memorial.
ii. Paribhogika stupa contained the buried bodily remains of Buddha.
iii. Bharhut stupa is situated in Uttar Pradesh.
questions.solution:
Only i and ii
Bharhut stupa is in Madhya Pradesh (not Uttar Pradesh), known for its early Buddhist reliefs and carvings.

questions.question: During which of the following rules did Buddhism get split into two schools - Hinayana and Mahayana in the fourth Buddhist council?
questions.solution:
Kushana
The Fourth Buddhist Council was held in 72 AD at Kundalvana, Kashmir, under the Kushan king Kanishka. It was led by Vasumitra, with Asvaghosha as his deputy, and marked the division of Buddhism into two sects: Mahayana and Hinayana.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The Shailendra rulers were great patrons of Buddhism.
Reason (R): They built the Borobudur stupa in Java, which is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
questions.option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.option_3: A is true, but R is false.
questions.option_4: A is false, but R is true.
questions.solution:
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
The Shailendra rulers of Java were devoted followers of Buddhism and extended great patronage to Buddhist culture and architecture. Their most remarkable contribution was the construction of the Borobudur stupa, one of the largest Buddhist monuments in the world, today recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.question: Stupas are a symbol of which of the following religions?
questions.solution:
Buddhism
Stupas were burial mounds prevalent in India from the Vedic period. Stupas typically consist of several elements: a circular base or platform, a hemispherical dome or Anda, a spire or Harmika, and a parasol or Chhatra. Sanchi Stupa in Madhya Pradesh is the most famous of the Ashokan stupas.

questions.question: The tall sculptures on the Bharhut Stupa are the depictions of
questions.solution:
Yakshas and Yakshinis
These are nature spirits in Indian mythology linked to prosperity and fertility. These figures symbolize the connection between the spiritual and natural worlds and showcase the integration of local traditions into Buddhist art.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Dhamek Stupa:
1. Dhamek Stupa is located at Kushinagar.
2. It was originally commissioned by Emperor Ashoka in 249 BCE.
3. The present structure of Dhamek Stupa was built around 500 CE, replacing the earlier construction.
Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect?
questions.solution:
1 only
Dhamek Stupa is not located at Kushinagar; it is in Sarnath. Both statements 2 and 3 are correct.

questions.question: Which of the following Indo-Greek kings was mentioned in the Buddhist text Milindapanho as Milinda?
questions.solution:
Menander I
The Milinda Panha is a dialogue between the Indian Buddhist sage Nagasena and the 2nd-century BC Indo-Greek king Menander I.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECT statement from among the following.
questions.option_1: 'Sanchi Stupa' is situated in Madhya Pradesh.
questions.option_2: 'Bavikonda Stupa' is situated in Andhra Pradesh.
questions.option_3: 'Dhamek Stupa' is situated in Uttar Pradesh.
questions.solution:
'Piprahwa Stupa' is situated in Sikkim
Piprahwa Stupa is located in Uttar Pradesh near the town of Piprahwa, close to the India-Nepal border. This site is renowned for its archaeological significance.

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest Stupa in India?
questions.solution:
Kesariva Stupa (Bihar)
It was discovered in 1958 during an excavation led by K.K Muhammed. Shanti Stupa (Leh) was built in 1991 by Japanese Buddhist Bhikshu Gyomyo Nakamura.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Ashvaghoshwa wrote the Buddhacharita, the biography of Buddha.
Reason (R): Ashvaghoshwa was the court poet of King Kanishka.
questions.option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.option_3: A is true, but R is false.
questions.option_4: A is false, but R is true.
questions.solution:
Both are true, and R correctly explains A
Ashvaghoshwa was the court poet of king Kanishka.
Other writers and books:
  • Nagarjuna - Mulamadhyamakara
  • Vasumitra - Mahavibhasha
  • Charaka - Charaka Samhita

questions.question:
Identify the Stupa based on the given characteristics:
1. Built by Mauryan emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE.
2. Located in Madhya Pradesh.
3. Declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1989.
questions.solution:
Sanchi Stupa
It is the oldest Stupa of the Buddhist period. Originally built with bricks by Ashoka, it was later enlarged during the Shunga dynasty with stone railings and gateways (Toranas). The Stupa enshrines relics of the Buddha. It is one of the best-preserved stupas in India and an important center of Buddhist art and architecture. UNESCO declared it a World Heritage Site in 1989.

questions.question: ______ was the first woman to be ordained as a bhikkhuni in Buddhism.
questions.solution:
Mahapajapati Gotami
  • Sanghamitta - Indian Buddhist nun and the eldest daughter of Ashoka
  • Sujata - fed Gautama Buddha a bowl of kheera (milk-rice pudding), ending his six years of asceticism
  • Venerable Dhammananda Bhikkhuni - first fully ordained Theravadin nun in Thailand

questions.question: With reference to Buddhist architecture, what does chaitya mean?
questions.solution:
Prayer Hall
It is a rectangular hall with a semi-circular apse at one end, which contains a stupa or relic chamber.
Other types of architecture:
  • Stupa - contained the Buddha's ashes
  • Vihara - Residence hall for the monks

questions.question: The rules made for the Buddhist 'Sangha' were written down in a book called
questions.solution:
Vinaya Pitaka
Buddhist teachings were divided into Three Pitakas at the First Buddhist Council in 483 BC.
  • Vinaya Pitaka - consists of rules of conduct and discipline applicable to the monastic life of the monks and nuns; compiled by Upali; written in Pali language
